newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris in bus talks with Mercedes, Iveco, Renault.
newsitem.headline: Azeris in bus talks with Mercedes, Iveco, Renault.

text.p: Azerbaijan's state-run automobile company Azerautonagliyyat is in talks with three West European automobile groups to revive its passenger bus production industry, a company official said on Monday.

Azerautonagliyyat Vice-President Kaviz Abdullayev told Reuters the company had held negotiations with officials from Mercedes-Benz, part of Germany's Daimler-Benz AG, last week and officials from Iveco, part of Italy's Fiat, and France's Renault were expected shortly as well.

He said the company, formerly Azerbaijan's Soviet-era automobile construction ministry, wanted the country to produce at least 3,000 to 5,000 small and large passenger buses per year for the domestic market in the first stages of manufacturing.
He said one or more of the Western automakers might form a joint venture with Azerautonagliyyat or one could be given rights to build and sell buses under government supervision.

"We are holding negotiations on various ways of cooperation. The main thing is to restore our bus industry, for which we have a sufficient technical base in the country. We just need certain types of technology and know-how," he said.
Azerbaijan produced buses at plants in Baku until the late 1980s, when the Soviet Union began to unravel.

He said a factory in the central city of Ganja, which was to have produced small passenger and cargo buses, had been "90 percent completed" by that time and could be readied for production in a short period of time.
"With the necessary help, the plant could be ready in six months to begin production," he said.
Abdullayev said any production would have to fully conform to European ecological and safety standards.
He said talks were also being held with the companies on helping re-organise the state-owned truck cargo transport networks and servicing parks.
Other foreign companies could also cooperate with Azerautonagliyyat, he said.
